newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures end mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures end mostly weaker.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended mostly easier on Wednesday, trailing weakness in New York overnight, although price losses were limited on the back of the yen's weaker trends, traders said.
Activity was lacklustre and trading was basically directionless.

The spot March gold expired flat at noon at 1,396 lots with 340 lots of deliveries. Other prices ranged from three to six yen per gram lower, with benchmark February ending down five at 1,377 yen. Spot gold was quoted at $347.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $347.30/80 in New York on Tuesday.
In gold futures, private investors were tending to buy on dips based on a perception that the yen will stay weak, while the buying was absorbed by trade house selling, the traders said.

Sentiment in the bullion market was bearish after a 25 basis points rate hike in the U.S. overnight. "The U.S. stock market is expected to be firmer as the rise had been factored into the stock market. So there will be little hope for fund money flowing into the gold market," one trader said.
Platinum futures ended down, also weighed down by trade house selling, the traders said.
Benchmark February platinum was down nine yen per gram at 1,456 yen.
Palladium futures moved within relatively narrow ranges for most of the day, not reacting to overnight news that the strike at a Russian mine had been averted.

Benchmark February palladium was off three yen at 565 yen. One trader said that palladium sales ahead of a hike of consumption tax from April was quite brisk in recent days in the physical market. Benchmark February silver futures was down 1.0 yen per 10 grams at 204.0 yen.
